title: Mechanosynthesis of the High Entropy Oxide Al2TiV2Y2ZrO15 and its Physicochemical Characterization
content: Recently, the search for new materials with adaptable properties has emerged. According to this, new materials such as high entropy alloys (HEAs) offer unique composition and remarkable properties. Besides, the field of high entropy materials has been broadened to include different groups of nonmetallic compounds known as high entropy ceramics (HECs), like oxides, carbides, borides, etc. [1]. Theoretical studies on high entropy oxides (HEOs) have revealed interesting insights into the material's electronic structure, bandgap and oxygen vacancies. These studies have shown that high entropy oxides can be tailored to have desired properties by altering the cation distribution and oxygen vacancies [2]. High entropy oxides (HEOs), despite their recent discovery in 2015, have gained significant research interest due to their unique structure stabilization mechanisms, ease of synthesis, and most importantly, their improved or nonconventional properties [3]. HEOs have possible applications as: catalysts, solid oxide fuel cells, lithium-ion batteries, electrocatalysis, etc. [4]. One of the major strengths of HEO-based materials is their ability to maintain phase purity despite their high compositional complexity, which offers an enormous composition space for property tailoring [3]. For the synthesis of HEO systems different synthetic methods have been reported, like wet chemical, sono-chemical, nebulized (NSP), flame spray pyrolysis (FSP), pulse-laser ablation, solid-state, sol-gel, auto-combustion, or epitaxial growth [5]. However, the mechanosynthesis has been gaining popularity because the process is carried out in the solid state, and it is easier to control the overall particle size distribution [6].
